name: Tam Coc food guide
summary: After the boat, lunch in Tam Coc is crisp rice, mountain goat, and nem Yên Mạc. Mountain snail comes in the rains, Hang Bụt is a meal you cook, and midday can be cá rô Tổng Trường.
body: Crisp rice at a Tam Coc restaurant is nếp hương with ruốc, eaten with mountain goat or with heart and kidney stir-fried with carrot, tomato, mushroom, and onion. The Ninh Bình plate is beef tenderloin and pork heart and kidney, with tomato, carrot, onion, and shiitake, poured on so the rice crackles. That beef plate is also set in the city or the old capital.

Lunch in the tourist area, or at a restaurant nearby, is that rice, mountain goat, and nem Yên Mạc. A Tam Coc day sets dê tái chanh, cơm cháy, and grilled goat at 11:45. Nem Yên Mạc is a Yên Mạc plate and a Yên Mô plate as well as this lunch.

Mountain snail comes out of the rock caves from April to August, grilled, stir-fried with tamarind, steamed with ginger, boiled, or in an onion salad. At Hang Bụt, visitors grill the perch they catch and cook crab soup and salted eggplant. One account puts the cave 1 km from chùa Bích Động. Another puts the visit in Sơn Hà.

Cá rô Tổng Trường is named at midday with mountain goat and crisp rice, and called a Ninh Bình specialty. Tổng Trường is the old name of xã Trường Yên in Hoa Lư, where the fish is cooked rang, rán, kho, or as canh chua with fried perch, pickled mustard greens, diluted nước dưa, tomato, and fried tofu. The culture office places the fish in the city or the old capital, and a Tet table has it kho tộ or rán giòn with hot rice.
specialtiesLead: Crisp rice, hill goat, nem Yên Mạc, mountain snail, the Hang Bụt meal, and cá rô Tổng Trường.

sections.heading: Tam Coc specialties
paragraphs: Cơm cháy is the crisp rice. Thịt dê núi, dê nướng, and dê tái chanh are the goat. Nem Yên Mạc is the fermented pork. The snail plates run from April to August. Cá rô nướng, canh cua, and cà muối are the meal visitors cook at Hang Bụt. Cá rô Tổng Trường is the midday perch.
